subject: Post-call: Eval playbook & regression watchlist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Saunders <tom.saunders@leafbank.com>, Emily Chen <emily@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Eval playbook & regression watchlist

Tom / Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we can get you a concrete evaluation and guardrails for model churn. High-level notes: 

- Scope: extractive/abstractive customer support summarization + policy-classification for LeafBank (sensitive PII redaction required).
- Key success metrics you called out: F1 on policy tags, ROUGE-L for short summaries, and latency under 300ms p50 for 8k prompt slices.

Recommended eval plan (short):
1) Run our customer-specific eval pack (attached: eval_playbook_v1.pdf + prompt_set_v2.jsonl). This includes ~1.2k labeled cases derived from your sample set.
2) Baseline models to test (suggested):
   - rw-13b-quant-v2 (preferred - best quality/cost balance for your workload)
   - rw-7b-fast-v1 (lower cost, lower-context latency-friendly)
   - fallback: rw-3b-std (for burst/failover)
3) Benchmarks: quick_bench_summary.csv attached; full run results are on the Drive link below. Please flag anything you want prioritized.

Regression & version-change guardrails (important):
- Watchlist triggers: any metric delta >3% absolute F1 or >5pt ROUGE-L vs pinned baseline should open an incident and block rollouts.
- Pinning options: we can pin to exact model build (e.g., v2026-09-28-rc3) per route. Pin is immediate and supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can elect route-level pinning for their account.
- Rollback: engineering can rollback a route to a prior model build within hours (we’ll outline timeline below).

Next steps I propose:
- Your team: confirm you can provide a 200–500 sample of the most important prompts (sensitive fields redacted) so we can run a targeted smoke test.
- Our team: run the eval pack against the three candidate models, capture diffs vs your baseline, and send a summarized regression watchlist.
- Schedule: can we book a 30-min follow-up the week of Oct 12 to review results and pin strategy?

Links/attachments:
- Eval pack & prompts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBqZx-example-eval-playbook
- Quick benchmark summary: attached (quick_bench_summary.csv)

If you want an immediate mitigation plan in the event of a regression, we can prepare a short runbook (emergency pin + canary policy) and deliver it within 24 hours. Please reply with permission to run on the 200-sample and availability for next week.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales (West)
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Saunders <tom.saunders@leafbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Eval playbook & regression watchlist

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the playbook. Quick heads-up: we started seeing a quality dip on production around Sep 29 after what our engineers think was an upstream model refresh. Two examples attached inline below (previous -> current).

Example 1 (policy tag):
- Prev: FIN-ACCOUNT-LOCK (correct)
- Now: ACCOUNT (too coarse)

Example 2 (summary):
- Prev: "Customer locked account after suspicious activity; advised reset and provided next steps."
- Now: "Customer contacted support about access issues." (lost key action items)

This matters — several cases where downstream automation misrouted tickets because of the coarser tag. We need an immediate mitigation: either pin back to the previous build or an emergency rollback. Can you put together ETA for a pin + run of the eval pack specifically against our recent production snapshot? Also, what do you do about SLA or credits when an update materially regresses quality?

Tom
Tom Saunders
Head of Trust & Safety, LeafBank
tom.saunders@leafbank.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0119

Folks — forwarding the thread from LeafBank. They reported a drop starting ~2026-09-29 that looks like a model build change surfaced in production. Summary: wrong policy tags and weaker extractive summaries for a subset of cases (examples attached in regression_examples.txt).

Can we do the following as priority: 
- Emergency mitigation: propose a pin to the last known-good build for LeafBank routes OR a rollback to the previous release. Which is faster?
- Evals: run the attached eval_playbook_v1 + their 200-sample production snapshot and compare diffs.
- Communication: I need a short note for Tom with ETA and the exact steps we'll take (pin vs rollback), and a clear statement about temporary impact and mitigation.

HubSpot: HS-789345 (LeafBank proof-of-concept). Drive link with initial artifacts is below. I attached regression_examples.txt and the eval pack to the Hub.

Attachments: regression_examples.txt

Thanks — Soojin

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 09 Oct 2026 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Eval playbook & regression watchlist — LeafBank regression examples attached

Looping in the infra and model ops runbooks. Short answers and plan: 

- Fastest mitigation: pin the LeafBank inference route to build v2026-09-28-rc3 (supported now). Pin is immediate (config flip) and will restore behavior seen prior to Sep 29. We can push that change within ~1 hour during business hours; outside business hours might take up to 3 hours for approvals.
- Rollback vs pin: rollback (redeploy previous build) is slightly slower (~2–6 hours depending on QA gating) and touches the global rollout. Pin only affects the customer route and is safer for multi-tenant hosted customers. Recommend pin for immediate relief.
- Eval plan: we will run the eval_playbook_v1 and the 200-sample snapshot against v2026-09-28-rc3 and current prod build v2026-10-01-rc2 and produce a diff report (CSV). ETA: initial diff report in 6 hours; full runbook + recommended canary policy in 18 hours.
- Next steps for comms: I can draft the note to Tom that outlines: what we will pin to, expected impact, and rollback criteria. Also include a short watchlist definition (metric deltas that trigger incident).

I've attached a short run plan (rollback_run_plan.md) and will start the eval runs once we get the 200-sample (preferable with some high-priority cases flagged).

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Redwood Inference
